citations.quote: The chapter then turns to the sources of budget deficits when Ricardian equivalence fails.
From the perspective of macroeconomics, fiscal policy is concerned with the overall levels and broad composition of taxes and government spending and their effects on the aggregate economy.
As one simple story, the fiscal theory of the price level answers: Money is valued because the government accepts money for tax payments.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Romer Ch.13 government intertemporal budget constraint and debt-sustainability dynamics; Ricardian equivalence under Ramsey households (tax timing irrelevant); contrasts with FTPL (Cochrane) where price level adjusts to back debt with future surpluses.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Fiscal Policy and Budget Deficits
